Jill Bolte Taylor holds the dual identity of a neuroscientist and a stroke survivor in recovery. She rose to global fame through her TED Talk and the publication of her book My Stroke of Insight. In 2008, she was named one of TIME magazine’s 100 most influential people in the world. After eight years of rehabilitation and two decades of using her own brain as a laboratory for exploration, she gained profound insights. She came to believe that the traditional notion of a "rational left brain" and an "emotional right brain" is incorrect. In fact, both the left and right hemispheres have regions responsible for thought and reason, as well as regions that govern emotion and feeling
